root_motivation: Verified 2026-09-13 during PRD-homeward-mcp-hub-deploy's real-environment AC checks (`tests/hub-deploy_ac3_search-pets-live.sh` against the live hub): - `sqlite3 ~/.local/share/homeward/homeward-ingest.db "select count(*) from canonical_records where json_extract(record_json,'$.location') is not null;"` → `0` (out of 185374 total rows). - `rescuegroups.rs`'s `map_animal`-equivalent function builds every `PetRecord` with `location: None,` unconditionally (line 635) — never reads whatever address/lat-lon fields the RescueGroups JSON:API response actually carries for the animal's org/shelter. - Two consumer-facing effects: (1) `search_pets`'s "coarse location" promise is unmet for every real result; (2) `search_pets(lat, lon, radius_km)` and `search_pets(postal_code)` — both explicitly documented tool parameters — can never match anything against live data, since `filter.rs`'s radius/postal-code filters read the same always-`None` field.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a RescueGroups API animal payload that includes an org/location relationship, When the connector maps it to a `PetRecord`, Then `location` is `Some(ShelterLocation { .. })` with real city/state (and lat/lon if the API provides them), not `None`.

Given the existing 185k-row production DB, When a backfill pass runs against already-ingested RescueGroups records (using stored `source_animal_id`s to re-fetch or re-derive location), Then a measurable majority gain non-null `location` (some source records may genuinely lack a location upstream — 100% is not required, but 0% must not persist).

Given a live `search_pets(lat, lon, radius_km)` or `search_pets(postal_code)` call after this ships, When run against real data, Then it returns non-empty results for at least one real query center known to have nearby shelters.

Given a fixture RescueGroups payload that includes org/location data, When the connector's mapping unit test runs, Then it asserts `location.is_some()`, so this regression class can't silently reappear.
